assumptions: glide with no distance: read as "the organism can glide" (run().feasible)
no organism named: start_from is empty (validation will ask for one, e.g. "a zebrafish ..." or "70% zebrafish 30% flying fish")
no stage stated for 1 criterion: adult assumed (say "as a larva", "at all stages" or "at 30 dpf")
no editable parameters stated: the optimizer has nothing to vary (say e.g. "vary the pectoral fin area from 0.02 to 0.08")
Lean constraints not mentioned: they hold anyway (constraints.lean is always "must-hold")

taxon_resolution.reason: "mouse" is placed in the clade table as Mus musculus. The spec carries it as `taxon`, so every law scoped to one of its clades is judged for it and a law scoped elsewhere is reported out of scope with its clade named. No reference parameter set exists for it, so no criterion can be evaluated and validation stays false.
next: organism_from_blueprint {blueprint} -- the full ontology hierarchy for a described organism, via organism-design/blueprint.mjs
taxon_resolution.what_is_missing: a reference parameter set (body-plan quantities and a growth track) for this clade; without one the engine can name the organism and check its laws, but cannot resolve a STATE, run a scenario or score it

scenario_criteria.how: pass the whole spec as `spec`; it runs the scenario modules at every requested life stage

routing.structures: organism-design/blueprint.mjs reads the structures named in the text and resolves them to Uberon/CL terms for the taxon; organism_from_blueprint brings the result into the studio
routing.laws: lean_check decides clade scope from the taxon and reports every law as holds / violated / out-of-scope / cannot-evaluate
routing.movement: locomotion_check -- how it moves, which no part list can settle: the scallop theorem, the cycle arithmetic and the Reynolds/Froude regimes
routing.world: ecology_check -- where the clade is recorded, what else is there, and what is recorded eating it. It will not predict exclusion without declared population parameters.

result.scope: A parse of the words, not an understanding of the request. Anything the rules do not cover is in `unparsed` and was NOT turned into a criterion; defaults the parser applied are in `assumptions`. Validation checks names, units and ranges against the scenario modules; it says nothing about whether the design can meet the criteria. An organism outside the engine's bundle is named and placed in a clade under `taxon_resolution`, which is a placement and NOT a parameter set: nothing dimensional is known about it here.
